confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from 5 web searches. These covered crowdsourced cost-of-living aggregators (restaurant meals, cappuccino, beer), a 2026 nightlife guide, and an Aperol Spritz price index. The aggregators disagree: an inexpensive meal ranged from about $8 to $14, and a mid-range dinner for two from about $16 to $57. I took values toward the upper-middle of the credible range and converted euro-quoted prices at roughly 1.16 USD/EUR, which is my own assumption. Cocktail and wine prices rest on one 2026 guide (cocktails about €7-9, wine about €4-7 a glass) plus spritz averages of about €3.7-4. I did not find a reliable Palermo-wide cocktail average, so the cocktail figure is a bounded estimate set against the beer price. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge for a July 2026 high-season window. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any booking pages or listings, so these are the least certain anchors. The FX observation is the latest RBA figure I could confirm (18 Nov 2026, 0.6720 USD per AUD) and was found through search, not by reading the RBA table directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Palermo restaurant and drink prices sit below the Italian average and below Rome (sources put restaurants about 14% below the national average). It is comparable to Naples and Catania. Summer accommodation is priced as a busy southern Italian leisure destination, not as a Rome or Milan-level city.
